description: Eval cases for the cursor-multitask routing skill. Each case tests whether the agent routes a fan-out / parallel task to the CORRECT engine (Cursor /multitask GUI, headless cursor-agent shell fan-out, Claude Workflow tool, cmux fleet, or serial-no-parallelism). The discriminating failure the skill prevents: a headless/terminal orchestrator reaching for /multitask, which silently no-ops because it is GUI-only (verified Cursor 3.3.2, 2026-06-05).

evals.name: headless-orchestrator-wants-parallel
evals.prompt: I'm running as an orchestrator in a cmux terminal pane (no Cursor editor open). I need to classify 40 files as relevant/irrelevant in parallel to save wall-clock time. Should I use Cursor's /multitask for this?
evals.expected_output: Must say NO — /multitask is an in-editor GUI command and silently no-ops in headless contexts. Should route to headless cursor-agent shell fan-out (background & + wait, or find|while read with --force --output-format json) OR the Claude Workflow tool. Should mention determinism / token accounting as the reason headless wins here.
evals.root_cause_tested: gui_misroute — the central mistake the skill exists to prevent

assertions.name: rejects_multitask_headless
assertions.description: Explicitly states /multitask will NOT work headlessly / is GUI-only

assertions.name: routes_to_headless_or_workflow
assertions.description: Recommends headless cursor-agent shell fan-out or the Claude Workflow tool instead

assertions.name: no_blind_multitask_recipe
assertions.description: Does NOT hand the orchestrator a /multitask invocation as if it would run

evals.name: human-in-cursor-editor
evals.prompt: I'm in the Cursor editor right now and I want to write tests, write docs, and run the type checker for the auth module all at once without queuing them, while keeping my main chat free for follow-ups.
evals.expected_output: This is the canonical /multitask use case: human in the editor, independent prompts, wants foreground free. Should recommend /multitask with the ||| separator in the Agents Window.
evals.root_cause_tested: correct_gui_use — skill should NOT over-correct and avoid /multitask when it IS the right tool

assertions.name: recommends_multitask
assertions.description: Recommends Cursor /multitask in the Agents Window

evals.name: sequential-dependency-no-parallel
evals.prompt: I need to (1) generate a database migration, then (2) run it, then (3) update the ORM models to match the new schema. Can I multitask these in parallel?
evals.expected_output: Must say NO to parallelism — these steps are sequentially dependent (each needs the prior step's output). Should recommend running serially in a single agent.
evals.root_cause_tested: false_parallelism — parallelizing dependent steps wastes tokens

assertions.name: rejects_parallel
assertions.description: States these steps are sequentially dependent and should NOT be parallelized

assertions.name: recommends_serial
assertions.description: Recommends running serially in one agent

evals.name: visible-multi-vendor-fleet
evals.prompt: I want to watch a Cursor agent, a Codex agent, and a Gemini agent each audit a different repo at the same time, visibly, so I can see their progress side by side.
evals.expected_output: Multi-vendor + visible + watchable = cmux fleet, not /multitask (single-vendor, in-editor) and not headless (not visible). Should route to /cmux-agents and reference /agent-routing.

assertions.name: routes_to_cmux
assertions.description: Routes to the cmux fleet / cmux-agents for visible multi-vendor work

assertions.name: not_multitask
assertions.description: Does NOT recommend /multitask (it is single-vendor, in-editor)

evals.name: ci-pipeline-batch
evals.prompt: In our CI pipeline I want to run lint, type-check, and the test suite as three parallel passes and fail the build if any returns nonzero. Best way?
evals.expected_output: CI = headless, scriptable, deterministic, needs exit codes. Should recommend headless cursor-agent shell fan-out (& + wait, capture exit codes / --output-format json), NOT /multitask (no CI surface).

assertions.name: routes_to_headless
assertions.description: Recommends headless cursor-agent shell fan-out for CI

assertions.name: mentions_exit_or_json
assertions.description: Mentions exit codes or --output-format json for deterministic CI gating

evals.name: interaction-with-agent-routing
evals.prompt: We're writing a collab kickoff for a sprint that has a big parallel data-gathering phase. How do agent-routing and parallelism fit together here?
evals.expected_output: Should distinguish the two axes: /agent-routing picks Cursor/Codex/Claude by task TYPE; cursor-multitask picks the parallelism ENGINE once it's known to be a fan-out. Should reference using both together.

assertions.name: distinguishes_axes
assertions.description: Distinguishes task-type routing (agent-routing) from parallelism-engine routing (this skill)
